topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and loss of growth control
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning outcomes, the historical hallmarks of cancer framework, and the central concept of lost growth control.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and survival signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades such as Wnt, Ras–MAPK, and PI3K–AKT drive sustained proliferation and survival signaling.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic alterations prevent cells from undergoing terminal differentiation in hematological malignancies and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Apoptosis evasion, replicative immortality, and stress response mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells overcome intrinsic tumor-suppressive barriers by disrupting apoptotic signaling, bypassing telomere shortening to achieve replicative immortality, and subverting p53-mediated stress responses.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss cancer cell metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect), diagnostic applications, and the epigenetic consequences of oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors induce new blood vessel growth via the angiogenic switch to overcome diffusion limits for oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the multistep process of metastatic spread, clinical detection via lymph nodes and circulating tumor cells, seed-and-soil compatibility, and the genomic characteristics of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising how diverse mutational pathways converge on shared hallmarks of cancer and wrapping up the session.
